speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool appearance alongside your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of drenching night sweats and significant weight loss alongside abdominal pain and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are highly concerning for a malignancy. Have you noticed any blood in your stool, or have you experienced changes in the size of your liver or spleen? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Lactate Dehydrogenase.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated.

speaker: Patient
text:
I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the neck swelling is painless and feels fixed; given the systemic "B symptoms" and lymphadenopathy, this is highly suspicious for lymphoma rather than an infectious etiology like Tuberculosis. I need to see the results from the blood tests I just ordered to assess for anemia or abnormal cell counts. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Lactate Dehydrogenase.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC confirms anemia with elevated white blood cells and a high Lactate Dehydrogenase level, which indicates high cell turnover, but the lab results do not support the specific diagnosis of Tuberculosis you requested. The combination of these B-symptoms, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and elevated LDH is most consistent with a lymphoproliferative disorder. REQUEST TEST: LDH (to confirm levels), T-Cell/ B-Cell Lymphoma Panel. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound, Chest CT, and Lymph Node Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: LDH: Elevated. T-Cell/B-Cell Lymphoma Panel: Pending. Abdominal Ultrasound: Splenomegaly detected. Chest CT: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Lymph Node Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index, combined with splenomegaly and massive lymphadenopathy, confirm a B-cell malignancy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL).
